Noturus gilberti Jordan & Evermann, 1889. Size: 100 mm (3.9") SL. Pronunciation: no two russ. Etymology: from the Greek notos, meaning back, and oura, meaning tail, in reference to the confluent adipose and caudal fins. Named to honour Charles H. Gilbert. IUCN Red List: Endangered (last assessed 2012).

Identification: long, slender body and flat head. White to orange triangle on the upper edge of the dusky to dark caudal fin. Short dorsal and pectoral spines. Olive or brown above, pale yellow or white below, with a light yellow or white edge on the dark fins.
North America: Upper Roanoke River (including Dan River) drainage in Virginia and North Carolina, USA. Type locality: Roanoke River at Roanoke, Salem, and Allegany Springs, Virginia.
Inhabits rocky riffles and runs of clear, swift, small rivers.
pH 6.2–7.0. Temperature 14–22°C (57.2–71.6°F). Highly oxygenated water is required.
Provide sand mixed with peat moss, PVC pipes, flat rocks and vegetation.
Readily feeds on live and frozen foods. Will also adapt to flake and prepared foods for the aquarium.
Suitable for a coldwater community tank. Ideal tank mates include small to mid-sized North American native fishes such as darters and shiners.
Breeding male with swollen lips, enlarged cephalic epaxial muscles, and a large bulbous genital papilla. Female with a papilla with a deep median groove ending in a small bump.

Spawning occurs in the months of May–August. It is difficult in the aquarium; however, it has been done when wild-caught specimens are added to aquariums with warmer temperatures than the river or drainage system they were captured from. There is no breeding report.
